title: Does ending in nine make a number divisible by nine?
description: Ninety nine thousand nine and one hundred nine are written as sums to see why one is divisible by nine and the other is not. Keeko's doubt is that one hundred nine is divisible by nine, because it ends in nine.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number is divisible by nine when every term of its place value sum is a multiple of nine, so one digit alone proves nothing. Watch for students who decide divisibility by nine from the units digit.

source: Explain why 99009 is divisible by 9, and why 109 is not even
video_script.why: The student knows that the units digit decides divisibility by two, five and ten and now sees why it cannot decide divisibility by nine.
video_script.substitution: Write each number as a sum and check whether every term is a multiple of nine.
video_script.anchor: a chart of place values with the digits of the number in its boxes, as the book writes a number as thousands, hundreds, tens and units
video_script.wrong_answer: one hundred nine is divisible by nine
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees that one hundred nine ends in nine, as ninety nine thousand nine does, and treats the units digit as the test for nine.
video_script.payoff_line: Ninety nine thousand nine is a multiple of nine

final_answer.value: 99009 is a multiple of 9; 109 leaves remainder 1, so a units digit of 9 proves nothing
final_answer.spoken: ninety nine thousand nine is a multiple of nine, and one hundred nine leaves remainder one, so a units digit of nine proves nothing

maths_rules: every term is 9 times a place value or zero, so the sum is a multiple of 9
99 = 9 x 11 and 108 = 9 x 12 are multiples of 9, so 109 is 1 more than a multiple of 9
a units digit of 9 does not decide divisibility by 9
video_script.design: Two place-value sums. In the first every term is nine times a place value. In the second the terms ninety nine and nine are multiples of nine and one is left over.

<bookmark mark='big'/>It is nine times ten thousand, plus nine times one thousand.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Then plus zero times one hundred, plus zero times ten, and plus nine times one.

<bookmark mark='sum'/>A sum of multiples of nine is a multiple of nine.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 109 = 99 + 10 = 99 + 9 + 1 = 108 + 1; 99 and 9 are multiples of 9; 1 is left over

<bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten is nine plus one.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Ninety nine and nine are multiples of nine, and one is left over.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 99009 is a multiple of 9; 109 leaves remainder 1, so a units digit of 9 proves nothing
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Ninety nine thousand nine is a multiple of nine.
One hundred nine leaves remainder one.
A units digit of nine proves nothing.
